content.text:
Consumer compiles EXIT=0, and the imported results are usable. Now compute SHA256 and sizes of the .lean, .olean, logs; check line count; check forbidden tokens; maybe run a source review grep. Also verify olean path.

Then send the report to the parent. But before that, let me reconsider the deliverable and whether we should strengthen the file further. The task: "在 S1895PaperO / S1927FullLogKummerUQ 上构造 R6 q-pilot anchor identification，或精确第一 missing；不要 fake anchor。"

Our file:
- constructs the reduced anchor + canonical times-mu + reduced identification on S1895PaperO and the S1958/S1927 package;
- precisely identifies the first missing as the paper-side definition;
- proves S1895's slot is self-identification (so not R6);
- no fake.

I think this satisfies "或精确第一 missing". But let me double-check the "精确第一 missing" content: Is the paper-side q-pilot F^boxplus-triangleright-x-mu-prime-strip genuinely the *first* missing, or is there something even earlier: the q_v-determination itself, i.e., the base q family? For S1895PaperO, the actual q_v are the bad-place q candidates `S1280ReductionClause.qParameter b` — actual. The q-pilot scalar is defined. What's missing is the *strip* (F^boxplus) associated to the q-pilot object. IUT III Def 3.8(i) defines the q-pilot object determined by q_v; the q-pilot F^boxplus-prime-strip is part of the F^boxplus construction (IUT II Cor 4.10(i)/(iii)). So the first missing is the paper q-pilot F^boxplus(-triangleright-x-mu) prime strip. Good.

Could the first missing instead be the operation-level Kummer/evaluation content (R3/R4) that would *make* the paper's q-pilot x-mu layer? R6 only concerns the anchor strip identification; the x-mu layer of the paper's q-pilot is part of the paper q-pilot strip. Since the paper q-pilot strip itself isn't defined, that's first.

One more check: Does `SourceFTimesMuPrimeStrip` correspond to `F^boxplus-triangleright-x-mu`? The module docstring says "IUT III, Theorem 3.11(i) and Remark 3.11.1(iii) work with F-turnstile-times-mu-prime-strips"; QPilotFTimesMuPrimeStripActual says "the source-facing type for an F^boxplus-triangleright-x-mu-prime-strip". So yes. Our doc uses that.

Now, potential issue: the file's first docstring says "the paper-side q-pilot F^boxplus-prime-strip (before or after the times-mu lift) is present" — the sentence is "no Lean definition ... is present", okay.

Let me compute the hashes. Use Get-FileHash SHA256. Also line count, olean size, and the tail of the compile log (EXIT=0). Then check the olean exists and is nonempty. Also maybe run `grep` for "sorry" etc. via the project's audit script pattern to report forbidden=0 (excluding docstring mentions). Let me do a source review:
`Select-String -Path file -Pattern "\bsorry\b|\badmit\b|^\s*axiom\b"` → will hit docstring line 67 ("No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`"). That's a benign comment hit. We can report "code forbidden=0; docstring mentions the words in the honesty note (standard practice)". Or use a stricter check excluding comment lines; not necessary. Maybe better to reword the docstring to avoid the literal tokens so a naive scan is clean? Other files (S1958) include "No sorry, admit, axiom..." and are accepted. Keep consistency.

Let's compute:
- SHA256 of S1960QPilotAnchorActual.lean
- SHA256 of .olean
- sizes
- line count
- EXIT (from log tail)
- consumer log tail
Also check the olean file path exactly.

content.name: run_code
content.arguments:
{"code": "
const r = await tools.pwsh({ description: "Compute S1960 artifact hashes and stats", command: `
$f = "D:\\lean\\tmp\\sheaf\\xif\\paper\\S1960QPilotAnchorActual.lean"
$o = "D:\\lean\\.lake\\build\\lib\\lean\\tmp\\sheaf\\xif\\paper\\S1960QPilotAnchorActual.olean"
$h1 = Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 $f
$h2 = Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 $o
"LEAN_SHA256=" + $h1.Hash
"LEAN_BYTES=" + (Get-Item $f).Length
"LEAN_LINES=" + (Get-Content $f | Measure-Object -Line).Lines
"OLEAN_SHA256=" + $h2.Hash
"OLEAN_BYTES=" + (Get-Item $o).Length
"OLEAN_PATH=" + $o
"COMPILE_LOG_TAIL:"
Get-Content "D:\\lean\\tmp\\sheaf\\xif\\paper\\S1960.olean.log" -Tail 3
"CONSUMER_LOG_TAIL:"
Get-Content "D:\\lean\\tmp\\sheaf\\xif\\paper\\_S1960Consumer.log" -Tail 3
"FORBIDDEN_SOURCE_REVIEW:"
Select-String -Path $f -Pattern "\\bsorry\\b|\\badmit\\b|^\\s*axiom\\b" | ForEach-Object { "$($_.LineNumber): $($_.Line.Trim())" }
`, workdir: "D:\\lean" });
console.log(r.kind === "foreground" ? r.stdout.text + "\nSTDERR:\n" + r.stderr.text : JSON.stringify(r));
", "description": "Report hashes, sizes, log tails"}
